sections.h2: How quickly can a Lodi house change hands?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: a retail listing, a for-sale-by-owner deal, or a purchase by an investor who pays cash and takes the house in its present state. The third route is usually the shortest in Lodi, because the borough's older housing needs work that a conventional buyer's lender may question.

A handful of items under your control set the real pace. Having them ready before you sign a contract trims days off the schedule.

  • A clean title and the recorded deed, plus finished estate paperwork if the owner has died.
  • The borough's resale certificate application, begun early because inspections need appointments.
  • Tax bills paid up and old building permits closed.
  • A decision on tenants: empty house at closing, or leases transferred to the buyer.

sections.h2: What is Lodi like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Lodi packs into 2.27 square miles of land in Bergen County, around 11,500 residents per square mile by the 2020 count. Voters created the borough on December 22, 1894, in the burst of borough-making that swept Bergen County, and mills along the Saddle River drew immigrant workers. Dye and chemical plants replaced the old textile works after the 1940s.

Many buyers commute. Route 17, U.S. Route 46 and Interstate 80 cross the borough, and NJ Transit routes 144, 161 and 164 carry riders to midtown Manhattan. Felician University has its campus in Lodi, and Lodi Public Schools run seven schools from pre-K to grade 12, among them Thomas Jefferson Middle School and Lodi High School. Bergen Arts and Science Charter School also enrolls Lodi students, and every Bergen County district can send students to the selective Bergen County Technical Schools programs. Immaculate Conception High School, an all-girls Catholic school founded in 1915, closed after the 2022-23 year.

Inspectors raise one local issue early: parts of the borough flood in heavy rain. Expect buyers to ask about wet basements and drainage, and keep any repair invoices where you can find them.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau record about housing in Lodi?
sections.html:
The Bureau's QuickFacts profile shows a borough where tenants outnumber owner-occupants, which shapes who sells and who buys.

  • The 2025 estimate is 26,187 people, nearly level with the 26,206 counted in 2020.
  • Only 42.4 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners (five-year survey ending 2024).
  • The middle value of a home that its owner occupies is $475,000, and the middle gross rent is $1,714.
  • Household income sits at a midpoint of $89,305.
  • About 39.5 percent of residents were born abroad, and 55.0 percent of those aged five and over speak another language at home.

In practice, many Lodi properties are one- and two-family houses with a rental unit, so buyers include small investors and families who plan to live in one apartment and rent out the other.

sections.h2: What local paperwork does Lodi require before a house sale?
sections.html:
The borough's Zoning Department issues permits for use and occupancy, and its forms list includes a Resale/New Tenant Certificate application. Call that office before listing to learn whether your sale needs the certificate and what the inspection covers, so a failed item does not push the closing date.

Rental owners face a second layer. The Fire Prevention Bureau inspects one- and two-family homes that the owner rents out rather than occupies, and it bills fees under the state fire code. If you are selling a landlord property, ask whether that inspection record is current.

sections.h2: What will a Lodi seller owe at closing?
sections.html:
New Jersey bills the seller for a realty transfer fee at the moment the deed goes on record. The Division of Taxation posts the rate table on its Realty Transfer Fee page, and a surcharge applies to sales above $1,000,000, beginning at one percent of the price.

Each seller also gives the settlement agent a GIT/REP form. A New Jersey resident signs the residency certification, known as GIT/REP-3. An owner who lives out of state, as many Lodi landlords do, files a different form and prepays income tax equal to no less than two percent of the sale price unless a listed exemption fits.

The Bergen County Clerk records the deed. Ask that office for its present recording charges, and have your attorney or title agent produce a written payoff and settlement statement ahead of the closing day.

sections.h2: How do Lodi property taxes and appeals work?
sections.html:
The assessor values each property as of October 1 of the preceding year. An owner who thinks the figure is too high can appeal annually before April 1; the borough says to phone the Bergen County Board of Taxation at (201) 336-6300 once the February postcard arrives and ask for a Petition to Appeal.

Improvements get assessed even without a permit. When an added assessment bill arrives, the borough says you must pay it in full whatever your view, and the window to appeal that bill closes December 1.

Before closing, ask the tax collector for the current-quarter payoff. Quarterly bills come due at the start of February, May, August and November, and the attorney splits the open quarter between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What should you prepare before a buyer inspects a Lodi house?
sections.html:
Begin with the basement and the lot, since drainage is the first thing an inspector probes in a borough where heavy rain floods low spots. Collect receipts for sump pumps, waterproofing, boiler service and roof work, and find the paperwork for past permits.

The assessor's office compares building permits with its records, and unpermitted work can still be assessed. Closing out old permits before you list prevents a surprise during the buyer's attorney review and gives a cash buyer less reason to cut an offer.

sections.h2: When is a cash buyer the right choice for a Lodi house?
sections.html:
Cash suits a property that needs more repair than a retail buyer will finance, an inherited house, or a building with tenants, liens or a damp basement that would stall a listing. A well-kept home with time on your side usually earns more through a listing, since cash offers price in the buyer's repair costs and risk.

Get at least one cash offer and compare it with an agent's estimate of list price minus commission and repairs. Ask each buyer who covers recording costs, whether the offer is as-is, and how tenants and open permits would be handled.

faqs.q: Is a resale certificate needed for a Lodi sale?
faqs.a: Lodi's Zoning Department issues a Resale/New Tenant Certificate and posts the application among its forms. Phone the department before listing to find out whether your property needs one.

faqs.q: What is the last day to appeal a Lodi assessment?
faqs.a: Appeals go to the Bergen County Board of Taxation before April 1 each year. A separate bill for an added assessment can be appealed until December 1.

faqs.q: Who covers the transfer fee on a Lodi sale?
faqs.a: The seller covers it. Your closing attorney can quote the exact amount, since the state's table depends on the price.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lodi house with tenants inside?
faqs.a: Yes, either with the tenants in place or empty. For a one- or two-family rental owned by someone who lives elsewhere, make sure the Fire Prevention Bureau inspection is current before closing.

faqs.q: Will flooding history hurt a Lodi sale?
faqs.a: It can lower offers, so disclose what you know. Parts of the borough take on water in heavy rain, and cash buyers typically accept the condition without demanding repairs.
